pr_body:
##### Summary
Fixes https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/14388.

##### Test Plan
1. Compile this branch and add the following option inside your `netdata.conf`:
```conf
[logs]
      severity level = info
```
2.  move content from `/var/log/netdata` to another directory, or remove them to avoid noise.
3. Start netdata and after few minutes run the command:
```sh
$ grep "ERROR :" /var/log/netdata/error.log | wc -l ; grep "INFO  :" /var/log/netdata/error.log | wc -l
0
653
```
4. Stop netdata and modify your `netdata.conf` for:
```conf
[logs]
      severity level = error
```
5. Start netdata and run next command:
```conf
$ grep "ERROR :" /var/log/netdata/error.log | wc -l ; grep "INFO  :" /var/log/netdata/error.log | wc -l
15
362
```
6. Keep the configuration like it is, because we need to take a look in the errors.

##### Additional Information

The eBPF plugin is using a different algorithm to parse args. The issue https://github.com/netdata/netdata/issues/14477 was already updated to address this issue.

<details> <summary>For users: How does this change affect me?</summary>
Describe the PR affects users: 
- Which area of Netdata is affected by the change? Logs
- Can they see the change or is it an under the hood? If they can see it, where? Yes, they will have less log events.
- How is the user impacted by the change?  They can control netdata logs.
- What are there any benefits of the change?  Flexibility for users.
</details>

issue_context.title: [Feat]: configuration option to disable INFO logs
issue_context.body:
### Problem

Setting configuration to

```
[logs]
debug=none
error=/var/log/netdata/error.log
access=none
```

i assumed that only ERRORS are being written to the console. ( I am using the docker image) 
However many plugins are giving many info logs, which can also be seen on the console.


### Description

It would be nice if INFO logs wouldn't be handled like ERROR logs.

A new configuration option would be nice, e.g.

```
debug=none
access=none
**info=none**
error=/var/log/netdata/error.log
```

so i can mute all info logs from the plugins.

### Importance

must have

### Value proposition

1. only get ERROR logs, when only ERROR logs are enabled
2. Immediately see on the console if there is an ERROR running netdata; no need to scroll up and down because INFO logs are "hiding" the error logs


### Proposed implementation

_No response_
comments: @thiagoftsm I think the proper solution here is to add a severity-level configuration option. I think we can start with error/info: info is the default, if error - no info level messages.

Just wondering - can log level be configured separately for each collector? e.g say you want info on one collector only and error on everything else.

Just wondering if that is something we might think about here too or if too complex for this specific discussion?

If by this specific discussion, you mean this issue then it doesn't belong here. I suggest opening a GH discussion and if you decide to do so please provide several examples of when/why you need that. Looks very questionable to me overall.

> Just wondering - can log level be configured separately for each collector? e.g say you want info on one collector only and error on everything else.

Technically speaking it is completely possible.
The first commits I pushed I addressed only netdata core messages, now I am starting working with collectors and I am already considering this possibility for the future.

> Just wondering if that is something we might think about here too or if too complex for this specific discussion?

On the other hand, what @ilyam8 said looks like the more correct here, considering this issue will be closed as soon we merge the PR open yesterday.

@andrewm4894 for 9 external collectors and all internal collectors the option `severity-level` will allow users to select the level they want per collector, please, take  look in the PR (you are a reviewer) and verify if I already delivered what you want.
We added the `severity level` option to `[logs]`. Setting it to `error` (or `err`) will remove all INFO messages from `error.log` and `collector.log` (starting from tomorrow nightly).
